Find the area $A$ of the finite region bounded between the curve $x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi y)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi y)$ and the $y$-axis, as shown above.

$A=$

worked_solution:
First, we find the $y$-intercepts of the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi y)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi y) & =0 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi y) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi y) \\ \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi y)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi y)} & =1 \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡(\pi y) & =1 \\ \pi y & =…,-\frac{3\pi }{4},\frac{\pi }{4},\frac{5\pi }{4},… \\ y & =…,-\frac{3}{4},\frac{1}{4},\frac{5}{4},…\end{aligned}
$$

From the diagram, we see that we want to find the area between the curve $x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi y)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi y)$ and the $y$-axis from $y=-\frac{3}{4}$ to $y=\frac{1}{4}.$ To find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{c}^{d}x(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-3/4}^{1/4}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi y)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi y))\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-3/4}^{1/4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi y)\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{-3/4}^{1/4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi y)}{\pi }|}_{-3/4}^{1/4}-{\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi y)}{\pi }|}_{-3/4}^{1/4} \\  & =-\frac{1}{\pi }[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{3\pi }{4})]-\frac{1}{\pi }[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{3\pi }{4})] \\  & =-\frac{1}{\pi }[\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})]-\frac{1}{\pi }[\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})] \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\pi }-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\pi } \\  & =-\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{\pi }\end{aligned}
$$

We obtained a negative number because the region lies to the left of the $y$-axis. So the area that we want is

$$
A=|-\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{\pi }|=\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{\pi }.
$$
